fail_closed_acceptance_check.logic: If d.RetStatus is a number, accepted iff RetStatus === 1. Otherwise falls back to Number(d.Value) > 1000 (a real recId, distinguished from Melipayamak's small numeric error codes). Any non-conclusive response is treated as failure — comment at sms.ts:90-99 states this is deliberately conservative: 'a message that wasn't sent must never be reported as sent'.
fail_closed_acceptance_check.smsTransportReady: api/src/lib/sms.ts:215-223 — requires MELIPAYAMAK_USERNAME + MELIPAYAMAK_PASSWORD + MELIPAYAMAK_BODYID_OTP all set before the OTP path will claim readiness; without it, OTP delivery would silently never arrive even though the request looks like a 2xx (guarded against per the comment).

steps: 1. Set the 3 env vars above in a non-production environment pointed at a real Melipayamak account with at least one approved pattern.

2. Trigger a real send through the code path, not a curl — e.g. call POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request with a real test-owned phone number (OTP path is synchronous, api/src/lib/sms.ts:227: 'if (job.template === otp) { await sendSmsNow(job); return; }' — no queue involved, so the HTTP response IS the send outcome).

3. Expect RetStatus === 1 in the (currently un-logged-to-caller) provider response; the code itself only logs it (api/src/lib/sms.ts:288-297: `log.info('ارسال شد → ...', { template, recId: data?.Value })` on success, `log.error` with `retStatus/strRetStatus/value` on failure) — the proof must read the API server's logs, not the OTP HTTP response body.

4. For a non-OTP template (e.g. booking_confirm), the send goes through the Job queue instead (api/src/lib/sms.ts:229-241, enqueue({kind:'sms', payload: job})). To prove it: after triggering, query `SELECT id, kind, status, attempts, result, last_error FROM jobs WHERE kind='sms' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;` (jobs table — api/prisma/schema.prisma:1235-1256) and confirm status transitions pending → done with no last_error, within the worker's poll interval (maintenance/jobs-drain, run every minute per cron/crontab:15).

5. Cross-check api/src/app/api/metrics output for rezervno_sms_sent_total{template=...} incrementing (api/src/lib/sms.ts:296 `metrics.smsSent.inc({ template })`) as a second, provider-independent confirmation signal.

6. Record the actual RetStatus/Value from step 3's log line in the launch log as the proof artifact — a 2xx HTTP response alone is NOT proof (meliAccepted() explicitly treats some 2xx-wrapped bodies as failure).

what_exists.self_hosted_backup_service: docker-compose.yml:137-160 — a dedicated `backup` container, `backup/Dockerfile` + `backup/entrypoint.sh`, running backup/scripts/backup.sh on a cron schedule (BACKUP_CRON, default '0 3 * * *' — docker-compose.yml:151) with BACKUP_KEEP retention (default 14 — docker-compose.yml:153) and optional immediate backup on container start.
what_exists.backup_script: backup/scripts/backup.sh — pg_dump --no-owner --no-acl piped through gzip to $BACKUP_DIR/rezervno_<timestamp>.sql.gz, verifies the file is >1KB (else deletes and exits 1 — treats an empty dump as a hard failure, not a silent success), rotates to keep only the newest BACKUP_KEEP files, ALSO tars the uploads volume separately (rezervno_media_<timestamp>.tar.gz, same rotation) because gallery photos live on disk, not in Postgres — restoring the SQL dump alone would give clean DB rows pointing at missing image files. Optionally uploads both to S3-compatible storage if S3_BUCKET/S3_ENDPOINT/S3_ACCESS_KEY/S3_SECRET_KEY are set (falls back to local-only, does not fail the backup, if `aws` CLI is missing).
what_exists.list_script: backup/scripts/list.sh — lists existing rezervno_*.sql.gz with size/date/count.
what_exists.restore_script: backup/scripts/restore.sh — takes a filename arg or defaults to the newest backup; 5-second Ctrl+C grace window; then `gunzip -c $FILE | psql -h $PGHOST -U $PGUSER -d $PGDATABASE` (a straight psql replay, not pg_restore — consistent with pg_dump's plain-text/gzip output, not a custom-format dump).

gaps_found: No automated restore drill exists anywhere in the repo (no CI job, no script that self-tests restore.sh against a scratch DB) — this violates CLAUDE.md rule §4 ('هر آرتیفکتِ تحویلی باید یک jobِ CI داشته باشد که واقعاً می‌سازدش') by the same logic that rule was written for: a backup script that has never been proven to restore is unverified, not working.

restore.sh uses plain psql replay of a pg_dump text/gzip file — there is no verification step inside the script itself (e.g. no post-restore row-count check or schema-version check) confirming the restore actually succeeded beyond psql's own exit code.

The media tar backup and the SQL backup are two independent files with independent timestamps — a restore drill must verify BOTH are restored from the SAME backup run (matching timestamp), or a media/DB mismatch (orphaned photo rows) is possible.
restore_drill_procedure_against_scratch_: 1. Stand up an isolated scratch stack (NOT touching the developer's already-running local Postgres per CLAUDE.md's ban on interfering with another agent's DB): `docker compose -p rz-drill -f docker-compose.yml up -d postgres redis` with a throwaway .env (random POSTGRES_PASSWORD).

2. Apply schema via the documented two-step path: `docker compose -p rz-drill exec api npx prisma migrate deploy` then `sh prisma/apply-sql.sh` (per docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:9-16) — OR, simpler for a pure-backup drill, seed via `npm run db:seed` to get non-trivial, identifiable rows.

3. Record a fingerprint before backup: `SELECT count(*) FROM reservations; SELECT count(*) FROM users; SELECT md5(string_agg(id::text,',' ORDER BY id)) FROM restaurants;` (or similar) — save the numbers.

4. Run backup/scripts/backup.sh inside the drill's backup container (or manually with the same pg_dump invocation) → produces rezervno_<ts>.sql.gz (+ media tar if UPLOADS_DIR populated with a test file).

5. Destroy and recreate the scratch Postgres data volume entirely (`docker compose -p rz-drill down -v postgres && docker compose -p rz-drill up -d postgres`) to simulate real data loss, not just an empty extra DB.
6. Run backup/scripts/restore.sh against the fresh empty instance, pointing BACKUP_DIR at the drill's backup output.

7. Re-run the step-3 fingerprint queries against the restored DB — PASS only if all counts/hashes match exactly. Also verify the media tar extracts and file bytes match (e.g. sha256sum) the pre-backup test file.
8. Time every step (backup duration, restore duration) to derive real RTO; note the DB size at drill time to make the number meaningful for future comparison.

9. Record PASS/FAIL with the actual command outputs (exit codes) in the launch log — a restore drill that isn't falsifiable against a known fingerprint is exactly the pattern CLAUDE.md rule §5 warns about ('تستی که وقتی موضوعش غایب است سبز می‌ماند، تست نیست').

new_scenario_to_add.payload_shape: { restaurant_id (uuid), date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:MM), party_size (int), preferences?, preorder?, guest?, notify_sms?, duration_minutes?, hold?, coupon_code?, gift_card_code?, gift_card_amount? } — schema defined at api/src/app/api/v1/reservations/route.ts:22-42 (reservationSchema).
new_scenario_to_add.auth_needed: Requires a valid customer JWT (authFromRequest at route.ts:52) or staff JWT with canManageReservations permission — a k6 test user must be seeded and logged in via /api/v1/auth/otp/verify first (with OTP_DEV_MODE=true in the load-test target env so the code is returned in the response instead of requiring real SMS, per CLAUDE.md's documented demo/OTP rule).
new_scenario_to_add.idempotency_header: Must send a unique `Idempotency-Key` per VU-iteration (route.ts:82-90) — otherwise concurrent identical keys across VUs would incorrectly replay one VU's cached response onto another, which would silently invalidate the load test's own throughput numbers, not just be unrealistic.
new_scenario_to_add.rate_limit_awareness: RULES.reservation = { max: 10, windowMs: 60_000 } per api/src/lib/ratelimit.ts (RULES.reservation) — enforced BEFORE body parsing (route.ts:65, 'اول ریت‌لیمیت، بعد پارسِ بدنه'). A naive high-VU test against one IP will mostly measure 429s, not the reservation transaction — the k6 scenario must either spread across enough distinct source IPs/X-Real-IP overrides (only trusted if the test target has TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=false, or hits a proxy that legitimately sets X-Real-IP) or explicitly budget for it: target concurrency should be designed as (max reservation attempts) ≈ 10 × (number of distinct test identities) per minute, and 429 rate should be tracked as a separate, expected metric (not folded into the error rate) — the same pattern loadtest/k6-scale-400k.js already uses for its own rl429 counter (loadtest/k6-scale-400k.js:20,66).

concurrency_retry_context.retry_logic: api/src/lib/reservations.ts:244-260 — up to 5 attempts, each wrapped in a Redis-based slot lock (acquireSlotLock, 8s timeout, line 241) plus a Postgres SERIALIZABLE transaction retry loop with randomized backoff (`20 * (attempt+1) + random*30` ms, line 255) on serialization errors.
concurrency_retry_context.when_CONCURRENCY_RETRY_409_is_thrown: api/src/lib/reservations.ts:261 (all 5 attempts exhausted with a non-serialization error or the loop falls through), :313 (after the outer catch re-verifies the slot really is full/conflicted and it ISN'T — i.e. genuinely 'try again', not a disguised SLOT_FULL) — this is the 409 CONCURRENCY_RETRY defined at api/src/lib/errors.ts:46.
concurrency_retry_context.why_this_matters_for_the_load_test: A write-path load test targeting a SINGLE popular restaurant+timeslot (the realistic worst case — many users racing for the same Friday 8pm table) will deliberately manufacture serialization conflicts; success criteria must therefore be 'exactly one 201 per contested slot + everyone else gets a clean 409 SLOT_FULL/TABLE_CONFLICT/CONCURRENCY_RETRY, zero 500s, zero double-bookings' rather than a flat p95 threshold — this mirrors the real incident already documented in the code's own comments (reservations.ts:266-274, 'یافته‌ی واقعیِ ممیزی — با تستِ زنده‌ی ۳۰ کاربرِ هم‌زمان روی یک میز پیدا شد').

load_test.target_p95: No project-wide reservation-specific p95 target is documented; the existing suite's global API target is p95<250ms / p50<150ms for READS (loadtest/k6-load-test.js:29-30, matching the header comment 'هدف: API<۱۵۰ms، P95<۲۵۰ms'). Recommend the SAME p95<250ms ceiling for the reservation WRITE path under moderate, non-contested load (distinct slots/restaurants), but a SEPARATE, looser bound (e.g. p95<1500ms, since each retry can add up to ~150ms backoff × 5) for the deliberately-contested single-slot scenario, and track 409 rate as a first-class pass/fail metric rather than an error.

db_migration_reversibility_07x.general_policy: docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:176-180 — 'Forward-only migrations: manual SQL migrations are not auto-reversible — write compensating scripts for risky changes and test restore from backup before schema changes.'

075.change: ALTER TABLE economy_ledger_entries ALTER COLUMN id SET DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(); — api/prisma/sql/075-economy-ledger-id-default.sql
075.reversibility: Trivially reversible (DROP DEFAULT) and non-destructive; idempotent already (no-op if the default already exists, per the file's own comment).

076.change: Adds 2 enums, 2 nullable-with-default columns (restaurants.provision_status, tenants.branch_limit), and a new staff_invites table — api/prisma/sql/076-restaurant-provisioning.sql
076.reversibility: Additive only (new table + new columns with defaults) — safe to leave in place even if the owning feature (SPEC-B provisioning) is rolled back at the app layer via a feature flag; a real rollback would need explicit DROP TABLE/DROP COLUMN scripts which do not exist today.

077.change: New menu_categories table + menu_items.category_id FK + is_out_of_stock column + a data BACKFILL from the existing text category column — api/prisma/sql/077-menu-categories.sql
077.reversibility: The backfill is the risky part — additive and idempotent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING per the file's own comment) but a rollback that needs to UNDO the backfill (e.g. if menu_categories data is judged wrong) has no compensating script. The legacy text column is deliberately kept as a mirror precisely so the old code path still works if the new one is rolled back at the app layer (comment: 'ستونِ متنیِ menu_items.category حذف نمی‌شود: میرورِ سازگاری برای مصرف‌کننده‌های موجود').

078.change: Adds menu_tag enum, menu_modifier_groups/options tables, menu_item_tags, menu_items.availability jsonb — api/prisma/sql/078-menu-modifiers-tags-availability.sql
078.reversibility: Additive only, no backfill of existing rows into these new tables (comment explicitly notes PKs have no server-side DEFAULT because 'هیچ backfill/INSERTِ خامی در کار نیست') — cleanly droppable if needed, low risk.

079.change: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX staff_owner_phone_unique_idx ON staff(phone) WHERE role='owner' — api/prisma/sql/079-staff-owner-phone-unique.sql
079.reversibility: DROP INDEX is trivial, BUT the migration has a MANDATORY pre-deploy precondition documented in its own header (lines ~55-60 of the file): the operator MUST run `SELECT phone, count(*), array_agg(id ORDER BY created_at) FROM staff WHERE role='owner' GROUP BY phone HAVING count(*) > 1;` against the target environment and confirm it returns ZERO rows before applying 079 to ANY real environment — the migration will hard-fail (unique_violation) on dirty data by design, and the file explicitly forbids any automatic cleanup of duplicate owner rows in the migration itself. This is a genuine rollback-runbook item: before applying 079 to production, this precondition query result must be recorded in the launch log (the file notes it was checked clean on 2026-08-27 against dev-only DBs — production has never been checked, since no production DB is reachable from any of these audit sessions).
079.founder_action: Run the precondition query against production BEFORE 079 is ever applied there, and record the (expected: empty) result.
